ui.title: Gargantua VR Educational Mode
ui.disclaimer: The visual effect is an educational approximation unless a full relativistic renderer has actually been implemented.

EVENT_HORIZON.title: Event horizon
EVENT_HORIZON.simple: The point of no return: nothing inside can send light or signals out to a distant observer.
EVENT_HORIZON.advanced: Causal boundary of the region from which no future-directed signal reaches infinity. Kerr: r_+ = GM/c^2 (1 + sqrt(1 - a*^2)).
EVENT_HORIZON.limitation: Not a solid surface; depiction is schematic and coordinate-dependent.

SHADOW.title: Black-hole shadow
SHADOW.simple: The dark patch you see: light paths that fall into the hole leave that part of the sky dark.
SHADOW.advanced: Apparent region of the observer's sky where backward-traced rays terminate on the horizon. Larger than the horizon. Schwarzschild: critical impact parameter b_c = 3*sqrt(3) GM/c^2.
SHADOW.limitation: Kerr shadow is slightly flattened and offset; the renderer outline is approximate.

ACCRETION_DISK.title: Accretion disk
ACCRETION_DISK.simple: A flat swirl of hot gas orbiting outside the black hole. It is not the black hole.
ACCRETION_DISK.advanced: Matter in near-circular orbits losing angular momentum; thin-disk temperature T ~ r^(-3/4). Inner edge near the ISCO.
ACCRETION_DISK.equation: T(r) ~ r^(-3/4) (far from the inner edge)

PHOTON_REGION.title: Photon region
PHOTON_REGION.simple: Where light can circle the hole on unstable orbits, creating a bright ring-like edge.
PHOTON_REGION.advanced: Kerr has a region of spherical photon orbits with radii depending on inclination, not one shell. Schwarzschild photon sphere: r_ph = 3GM/c^2.
PHOTON_REGION.limitation: Drawn as a ring approximation, not the exact Kerr photon region.

LENSING.title: Gravitational lensing
LENSING.simple: Gravity bends light, so we can see the far side of the disk bent over the top of the hole.
LENSING.advanced: Null geodesics curve in curved spacetime. Weak-field deflection angle = 4GM/(c^2 b).
LENSING.limitation: Strong-field deflection in the app is approximated unless geodesics are integrated.

DOPPLER.title: Doppler shift
DOPPLER.simple: Gas moving toward you looks bluer, gas moving away looks redder.
DOPPLER.advanced: Frequency ratio g = 1/(gamma (1 - beta cos theta)), theta from motion to line of sight.
DOPPLER.limitation: Not all red/blue seen near a black hole is Doppler; redshift and beaming are separate.

BEAMING.title: Relativistic beaming
BEAMING.simple: Fast-moving gas looks brighter when heading toward you and dimmer when moving away.
BEAMING.advanced: Observed specific intensity scales as g^3 (I_nu/nu^3 invariant); bolometric ~ g^4.
BEAMING.limitation: Applied with the approximate g factor; separate from color shift.

REDSHIFT.title: Gravitational redshift
REDSHIFT.simple: Light climbing out of strong gravity arrives with lower frequency.
REDSHIFT.advanced: For a static emitter in Schwarzschild: nu_obs/nu_emit = sqrt(1 - r_s/r). Kerr/orbiting emitters need the full factor.
REDSHIFT.limitation: Shown as observed-frequency visualization (false color), not literal photon color.

FRAME_DRAGGING.title: Frame dragging
FRAME_DRAGGING.simple: A spinning black hole twists the geometry around it so nothing nearby can stay at rest relative to distant stars.
FRAME_DRAGGING.advanced: Inertial frames are dragged with angular velocity omega. Kerr equatorial: omega = 2GJ r / ((r^2+a^2)^2 - Delta a^2 sin^2 theta). Weak field: omega = 2GJ/(c^2 r^3).
FRAME_DRAGGING.limitation: Visualization is an analogy; space is not literally flowing.

ERGOSPHERE.title: Ergosphere
ERGOSPHERE.simple: A region outside the horizon where standing still is impossible; everything is dragged around.
ERGOSPHERE.advanced: Region between r_+ and r_E = GM/c^2 (1 + sqrt(1 - a*^2 cos^2 theta)). Equatorial r_E = 2GM/c^2.
ERGOSPHERE.limitation: Outer boundary exact in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates; depiction schematic.

TIME_DILATION.title: Time dilation
TIME_DILATION.simple: Clocks at different places or speeds tick at different rates. Time does not simply 'stop' at the horizon.
TIME_DILATION.advanced: Static observer: dtau/dt = sqrt(1 - r_s/r) relative to infinity. An infalling observer crosses the horizon in finite proper time.

lessons.title: Safe observation distance
lessons.simple: You are watching from a safe distance. Nothing here can hurt you.
lessons.advanced: Observer at r_obs >> r_+. All views are static; no forced motion.

lessons.title: Mass
lessons.simple: A black hole's gravity depends on its mass. Mass sets the size of everything else.
lessons.advanced: Characteristic length GM/c^2; r_s = 2GM/c^2 for spin 0. 1 Msun gives r_s of about 2.95 km.

lessons.title: The shadow
lessons.simple: The dark circle is not the black hole itself. It is a shadow made by bent light.
lessons.advanced: Rays traced backward from the observer that end on the horizon define the shadow.

lessons.title: Shadow vs event horizon
lessons.simple: The shadow looks bigger than the horizon. They are different things.
lessons.advanced: Schwarzschild shadow radius 3*sqrt(3) GM/c^2 (about 2.6 r_s) versus r_s.

lessons.title: Event horizon
lessons.simple: The event horizon is a boundary. Past it, light cannot escape to far-away observers.

lessons.title: No solid surface
lessons.simple: There is no hard surface at the horizon. You would not hit a wall.
lessons.advanced: The horizon is a null surface in spacetime, not a material object.

lessons.title: Accretion disk
lessons.simple: The glowing ring is hot gas orbiting outside the black hole.
lessons.advanced: Thin-disk model; hotter inside, cooler outside; orbital direction shown.

lessons.title: Far side of the disk
lessons.simple: Light from the far side of the disk is bent over the top of the hole to reach you.
lessons.advanced: Backward ray tracing from the observer reaches the far-side disk via strongly curved geodesics.

lessons.title: Gravitational lensing
lessons.simple: Gravity bends light. The disk is not bending; its image is displaced.
lessons.advanced: Null geodesics in curved spacetime; weak-field deflection 4GM/(c^2 b).

lessons.title: Photon region
lessons.simple: Some light can orbit the black hole briefly before escaping or falling in.
lessons.advanced: Schwarzschild r_ph = 3GM/c^2. Kerr has a photon region, not a single shell.

lessons.title: Kerr spin
lessons.simple: Real black holes can spin. Spin is described by a number between 0 and 1.
lessons.advanced: a* = a/M = cJ/(GM^2), 0 <= a* < 1. Not a rotating solid ball.

lessons.title: Frame dragging
lessons.simple: A spinning black hole drags the geometry around it along. This picture is an analogy.
lessons.advanced: omega is the angular velocity of locally non-rotating observers.

lessons.title: Doppler shift
lessons.simple: Gas moving toward you is bluer, gas moving away is redder.

lessons.title: Relativistic beaming
lessons.simple: Fast gas moving toward you also looks brighter. That is separate from color.

lessons.title: Gravitational redshift
lessons.simple: Light leaving strong gravity loses energy and shifts toward red.
lessons.advanced: nu_obs/nu_emit = sqrt(1 - r_s/r) for static emitters.

lessons.title: Time dilation
lessons.simple: Clocks run at different rates in different gravity. Time does not stop at the horizon.
lessons.advanced: dtau/dt = sqrt(1 - r_s/r) for static observers; infalling crosses horizon in finite proper time.

lessons.title: Science vs approximation
lessons.simple: Compare Newtonian gravity, the app's approximation, and a full relativistic model.
lessons.advanced: Newtonian gravity does not predict lensing of this strength, a shadow, or a photon region.

lessons.title: Quiz
lessons.advanced: Ten questions covering the concepts above.

quiz.question: What is the event horizon?
options: A solid surface of the black hole
A boundary beyond which light cannot escape to a distant observer
The dark region seen in images
quiz.explanation: It is a causal boundary, not a material surface.

quiz.question: What is the black-hole shadow?
options: A dark patch on the sky from captured light rays and strong light bending
quiz.explanation: The shadow is larger than the horizon and depends on observer and spin.

quiz.question: What is the accretion disk?
options: Hot matter orbiting outside the black hole
quiz.explanation: It is ordinary matter outside the hole.

quiz.question: Why can the far side of the disk appear above the black hole?
options: Light from the far side is bent around the hole toward the observer
A camera trick unrelated to physics
The hole pushes the disk up
quiz.explanation: The IMAGE is displaced by gravitational light bending.

quiz.question: What is gravitational lensing?
options: Bending of light paths by gravity
quiz.explanation: Mass curves spacetime and light follows that curvature.

quiz.question: What is frame dragging?
options: A rotating mass altering the surrounding spacetime so inertial frames are dragged

quiz.question: What is Doppler shift?
options: Change in observed frequency due to relative motion
quiz.explanation: Doppler is distinct from gravitational redshift and beaming.

quiz.question: What is gravitational redshift?
options: Light losing frequency climbing out of a gravitational field as seen by a distant observer
quiz.explanation: It is a gravity effect, separate from motion.

quiz.question: What is the photon region?
options: Region of unstable photon orbits; in Kerr it is not one simple sphere
quiz.explanation: Schwarzschild has the photon sphere at 3GM/c^2; Kerr is more complex.

quiz.question: Why is the Quest visualization an approximation?
options: It uses simplified formulas and real-time shortcuts rather than full relativistic ray tracing and fluid simulation
quiz.explanation: Performance limits require simplification; each feature is labeled by accuracy.

comparison.title: A. Newtonian reference
comparison.text: Gravity as a force on matter. No horizon, no shadow, no photon region; light not bent at this strength.

comparison.title: B. Relativistic-inspired approximation
comparison.text: Real-time shader with approximate deflection, Doppler, beaming and redshift factors.
comparison.limit: Not a full geodesic integration; shadow and photon region are approximated.

comparison.title: C. Higher-quality renderer (not implemented)
comparison.text: Full Kerr geodesic ray tracing, offline or on desktop GPU. Placeholder.
